questions.question: A company runs a web application on EC2 instances behind an ALB. Traffic spikes unpredictably during business hours. Which solution provides the MOST cost-effective way to handle variable load while maintaining high availability?
options: Provision a fixed large EC2 instance to handle peak traffic
Use an Auto Scaling Group with a target tracking policy based on CPU utilization
Use Reserved Instances sized for peak load
Deploy multiple regions with Route 53 failover routing
questions.explanation: An Auto Scaling Group with target tracking policy automatically adds/removes instances based on actual demand. This is the most cost-effective approach — you only pay for capacity when needed. Target tracking keeps a metric (CPU, request count) near a desired value, scaling in and out automatically.

questions.question: A company needs a database that can scale to handle millions of requests per second with single-digit millisecond latency. The data is key-value structured with no complex joins required. Which AWS service is BEST suited?
options: Amazon RDS Aurora
Amazon Redshift
Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon ElastiCache for Redis
questions.explanation: DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. It's purpose-built for key-value and document workloads requiring massive throughput. ElastiCache is in-memory only (no persistence), while RDS and Redshift are relational databases not suited for millions of RPS at this latency.

questions.question: An application stores user-uploaded files in S3. Files are frequently accessed for the first 30 days, rarely accessed for the next 60 days, then never needed again. Which S3 lifecycle configuration minimizes storage cost?
options: Store all objects in S3 Standard indefinitely
Transition to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days, then delete after 90 days
Immediately store in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering for all objects
questions.explanation: S3 Standard-IA (Infrequent Access) charges lower storage rates but higher retrieval fees — ideal for rarely accessed data that still needs quick retrieval. Transitioning after 30 days and deleting after 90 days (30+60) matches the access pattern exactly. S3 Glacier would add retrieval delays. Intelligent-Tiering has monitoring fees on every object.

questions.question: A company wants to ensure its application remains available even if an entire AWS Availability Zone fails. Which architecture pattern achieves this?
options: Deploy all EC2 instances in a single AZ with snapshots enabled
Use CloudFront with S3 as origin
Distribute instances across at least two AZs behind an ALB with health checks
Enable EC2 Auto Recovery for all instances
questions.explanation: Distributing instances across multiple Availability Zones ensures that an AZ failure only affects a portion of the fleet. The ALB with health checks automatically routes traffic to healthy instances. EC2 Auto Recovery only restarts the same instance in the same AZ. CloudFront+S3 is for static content. Single-AZ is a single point of failure.

questions.question: A solutions architect needs to allow an EC2 instance to read objects from an S3 bucket. What is the MOST secure way to grant this permission?
options: Embed AWS access keys directly in the application code
Store access keys in an environment variable on the EC2 instance
Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance with the required S3 permissions
Create an IAM user and put the credentials in /etc/aws/credentials
questions.explanation: IAM roles attached to EC2 instances provide temporary credentials that are automatically rotated — no long-term keys to manage or accidentally expose. The application uses the instance metadata service (IMDS) to retrieve short-lived credentials. Hardcoding or storing access keys in any form is a security anti-pattern.

questions.question: A company runs an RDS MySQL database and wants to improve read performance for a reporting application without impacting the primary database. What should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Enable Multi-AZ deployment
Create a Read Replica of the RDS instance
Scale up the primary RDS instance to a larger type
Enable RDS automatic backups with a longer retention period
questions.explanation: RDS Read Replicas create an asynchronous copy of the primary database that serves read traffic. The reporting application connects to the replica endpoint, offloading queries from the primary. Multi-AZ is for failover/HA, not read scaling. Scaling up the primary helps writes but doesn't distribute reads. Backups are for recovery, not performance.

questions.question: An application in a private subnet needs to download software packages from the internet. No inbound connections from the internet should be allowed. What is the CORRECT solution?
options: Attach an Internet Gateway directly to the private subnet
Create a NAT Gateway in a public subnet and update the private subnet route table to point 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT Gateway
Assign an Elastic IP to each EC2 instance in the private subnet
Create a VPC peering connection to another VPC with internet access
questions.explanation: A NAT Gateway in a public subnet allows instances in private subnets to initiate outbound internet connections while blocking all inbound connections. The route table in the private subnet directs internet-bound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) to the NAT Gateway, which translates addresses and forwards the traffic through the Internet Gateway in the public subnet.

questions.question: A company wants to serve static website content globally with low latency. The content changes infrequently. Which combination provides the MOST cost-effective solution?
options: Multiple EC2 instances in different regions with Route 53 latency routing
An S3 bucket configured for static website hosting with CloudFront distribution in front
ALB with multiple EC2 instances across AZs
AWS Global Accelerator with an S3 origin
questions.explanation: S3 static website hosting with CloudFront is the canonical low-cost, globally distributed static content solution. CloudFront caches content at edge locations worldwide for ultra-low latency. S3 storage is cheap and highly durable. No servers to manage. Global Accelerator is designed for dynamic content, not static asset caching.

questions.question: A Lambda function needs to access a private RDS database without exposing the database to the public internet. Which configuration achieves this?
options: Enable RDS public accessibility and whitelist the Lambda IP address
Deploy the Lambda function inside the same VPC as RDS, in a private subnet, with appropriate security group rules
Use Lambda@Edge to access RDS through CloudFront
Create a VPC endpoint for RDS and configure Lambda to use it
questions.explanation: Deploying Lambda in the same VPC as RDS (with VPC configuration on the Lambda function) allows private communication. The Lambda function gets an ENI in the VPC subnet, and security groups control access. RDS stays private with no public endpoint needed. Note: There is no VPC Gateway Endpoint for RDS — Interface endpoints exist for specific APIs, not RDS TCP access.

questions.question: An e-commerce application needs to process orders asynchronously. When an order is written, multiple downstream services (inventory, shipping, email) must each receive a copy. Which AWS architecture handles this BEST?
options: Write directly to each downstream service's SQS queue from the order service
Use SNS to publish to a topic; each downstream service subscribes with its own SQS queue (fan-out pattern)
Store orders in DynamoDB and have each service poll for new records
Use Kinesis Data Streams with a single consumer
questions.explanation: The SNS fan-out pattern publishes a single message to an SNS topic, which delivers it to multiple SQS queues (one per subscriber). Each downstream service reads from its own queue independently, decoupling producers from consumers. Writing to each queue directly creates tight coupling. DynamoDB polling is inefficient. Kinesis supports fan-out but is designed for streaming data, not simple message queuing.

questions.question: A company needs to connect its on-premises data center to AWS with consistent, dedicated bandwidth and low latency for transferring large amounts of data. Which service should they use?
options: AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the public internet
AWS Direct Connect
AWS Transit Gateway with VPN attachments
AWS Client VPN
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private network connection between on-premises and AWS, bypassing the public internet. This delivers consistent bandwidth, lower latency, and reduced data transfer costs for large volumes. Site-to-Site VPN runs over the public internet and has variable latency. Transit Gateway aggregates multiple connections but doesn't provide a dedicated physical link.

questions.question: A company runs an application where users upload large files that need to be stored durably but retrieved very rarely (once a year at most). Cost minimization is the primary requirement. Which S3 storage class should be used?
options: S3 Standard
S3 Standard-IA
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 One Zone-IA
questions.explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost S3 storage class (~$0.00099/GB-month) — designed for data accessed once or twice per year with a retrieval time of up to 12 hours. Ideal for long-term archival where cost trumps retrieval speed. S3 Standard-IA charges higher per-GB rates. One Zone-IA sacrifices redundancy. Standard is the most expensive per GB.

questions.question: An application uses SQS to process tasks. Some messages are consistently failing to process and causing delays. The architecture must prevent bad messages from blocking valid ones while preserving failed messages for investigation. What should be implemented?
options: Increase the SQS message retention period to 14 days
Configure a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) with a maxReceiveCount, and set up an alarm on the DLQ depth
Enable SQS FIFO ordering to process messages in order
Increase the visibility timeout to give more processing time
questions.explanation: A Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) receives messages that fail processing after maxReceiveCount attempts. This prevents a 'poison pill' message from blocking other processing. The DLQ allows developers to inspect failed messages without losing them. Setting a CloudWatch alarm on DLQ depth provides operational visibility. FIFO ordering and visibility timeout don't handle persistently failing messages.

questions.question: A web application needs to store user session state in a highly available, low-latency datastore that survives EC2 instance failures. Which service is MOST appropriate?
options: EC2 instance store
EBS volume attached to each EC2 instance
Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with Multi-AZ enabled
Amazon RDS with read replicas
questions.explanation: ElastiCache for Redis provides sub-millisecond latency session storage external to EC2 instances, so sessions survive instance failures. With Multi-AZ, Redis automatically fails over to a replica if the primary fails. Instance store and EBS are instance-local — when the instance dies, the session is lost. RDS is a relational database suited for persistent structured data, not low-latency session caching.

questions.question: A company needs to migrate 50 TB of data to S3. Their internet connection is 100 Mbps and is needed for business operations. The data must be transferred within 5 days. Which service should they use?
options: AWS DataSync over the existing internet connection
S3 Transfer Acceleration
AWS Snowball Edge
Direct Connect with 1 Gbps port
questions.explanation: 50 TB over 100 Mbps would take approximately 46 days at full utilization. AWS Snowball Edge is a physical device shipped to your location — you load data locally and ship it back to AWS for ingestion into S3, completing the transfer within the 5-day requirement. DataSync and S3 Transfer Acceleration still use the internet connection. Direct Connect provisioning takes weeks.

questions.question: An application requires strong read consistency for a DynamoDB table. Which read operation provides this?
options: Eventually consistent reads using GetItem with default settings
Strongly consistent reads using GetItem with ConsistentRead=true
Using a DynamoDB Global Secondary Index with ConsistentRead
DynamoDB Streams with Lambda trigger
questions.explanation: Setting ConsistentRead=true on DynamoDB read operations (GetItem, Query, Scan) ensures the response reflects all writes that received a successful response before the read. Strongly consistent reads cost twice the RCU of eventually consistent reads. Note: GSIs only support eventually consistent reads — you cannot do strongly consistent reads against a GSI.

questions.question: A company needs to allow users to upload files directly to S3 from a browser without routing traffic through application servers. The upload URL must expire after 15 minutes. Which approach should be used?
options: Make the S3 bucket publicly writable
Generate a presigned URL on the server and return it to the client for direct upload
Use API Gateway with a Lambda proxy to forward uploads to S3
Enable CORS on the S3 bucket and use the bucket's public endpoint
questions.explanation: S3 presigned URLs allow temporary, time-limited access to perform specific S3 operations (including PUT for uploads) using the generating identity's permissions. The server generates the URL with an expiration (up to 7 days) and returns it to the client. The browser uploads directly to S3, bypassing application servers entirely. This reduces load on app servers and eliminates double-transfer overhead.

questions.question: A solutions architect is designing a system where multiple AWS accounts need to share a single centralized outbound internet connection. Which service achieves this at scale?
options: VPC peering between all accounts
AWS Transit Gateway with a shared VPC containing a NAT Gateway
Each account deploys its own NAT Gateway
AWS PrivateLink from each account to a central egress VPC
questions.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a cloud router connecting multiple VPCs and accounts. A centralized egress VPC with a NAT Gateway is attached to the Transit Gateway, and all other VPCs route internet-bound traffic through it. This avoids deploying NAT Gateways in each account (cost savings) and centralizes egress monitoring. VPC peering doesn't support transitive routing.

questions.question: An application uses EC2 instances that need access to an S3 bucket in the same region. To minimize data transfer costs and avoid traffic going over the public internet, what should be configured?
options: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration
Create a Gateway VPC Endpoint for S3 and update the route table
Set up an AWS Direct Connect link between EC2 and S3
Use a NAT Gateway to route S3 traffic
questions.explanation: A Gateway VPC Endpoint for S3 routes traffic from EC2 to S3 entirely within the AWS network, without traversing the internet or requiring a NAT Gateway. This is free of charge and keeps S3 traffic private. It requires adding a route to the subnet route table. NAT Gateway charges per GB for traffic it handles — VPC endpoints eliminate this cost for S3 and DynamoDB.

questions.question: A company wants to automatically remediate non-compliant S3 bucket configurations (e.g., buckets without encryption enabled) as soon as they are detected. Which combination of services enables this?
options: CloudWatch Events + Lambda to periodically check all buckets
AWS Config rule with an automatic remediation action using SSM Automation
AWS Trusted Advisor with SNS notifications
AWS Security Hub with manual remediation workflows
questions.explanation: AWS Config continuously monitors resource configurations and evaluates them against rules. When a Config rule detects non-compliance, it can trigger an automatic remediation action (backed by an SSM Automation document) to fix the configuration. This provides near-real-time detection and automatic remediation without custom Lambda code for polling.

questions.question: An EC2 instance in a public subnet needs to be accessible via SSH from the internet, but only from a specific corporate IP range (203.0.113.0/24). Where should this restriction be configured?
options: In the S3 bucket policy controlling the SSH key file
In the EC2 instance's Security Group as an inbound rule allowing port 22 from 203.0.113.0/24
In the VPC's Internet Gateway route table
Using AWS WAF to block all other IPs
questions.explanation: Security Groups are stateful firewalls at the instance level. Adding an inbound rule allowing TCP port 22 from source 203.0.113.0/24 restricts SSH to only that IP range. Security Groups default to deny all inbound, so only explicitly allowed traffic reaches the instance. WAF operates at layer 7 HTTP, not SSH. Route tables control IP routing, not access control.

questions.question: A data analytics pipeline ingests hundreds of thousands of events per second from IoT devices. Events need to be processed in real time and stored in S3 for later batch analysis. Which AWS service should anchor the ingestion layer?
options: Amazon SQS Standard Queue
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon SNS with S3 subscription
Amazon MQ with ActiveMQ
questions.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams is designed for real-time streaming of massive event volumes, supporting hundreds of thousands of records per second per shard. Data can be processed by Kinesis Data Analytics or Lambda in real time while Kinesis Data Firehose delivers a copy to S3. SQS doesn't maintain ordering and isn't designed for real-time analytics pipelines at this scale. SNS doesn't persist data.

questions.question: A company needs to encrypt data in S3 with keys they fully control and audit all key usage. Which S3 encryption option meets these requirements?
options: SSE-S3 (Server-Side Encryption with S3-managed keys)
SSE-KMS using an AWS-managed key (aws/s3)
SSE-KMS using a Customer Managed Key (CMK) in AWS KMS
Client-side encryption with a locally stored key
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS with a Customer Managed Key (CMK) lets you define key policies, rotate keys, audit all usage in CloudTrail, and enable/disable the key. SSE-S3 uses AWS-managed keys with no customer control or visibility. The AWS-managed KMS key (aws/s3) provides some audit trail but you cannot manage the key policy or disable it. Client-side encryption requires customers to manage the entire encryption lifecycle.

questions.question: An application tier running on EC2 receives traffic from an ALB. The EC2 instances need to talk to a backend RDS database. Which security group configuration CORRECTLY applies least privilege?
options: Allow all inbound on the EC2 SG; allow all inbound on the RDS SG
EC2 SG: allow inbound on app port from ALB SG; RDS SG: allow inbound on DB port from EC2 SG
EC2 SG: allow inbound from 0.0.0.0/0; RDS SG: allow inbound from VPC CIDR
Configure both SGs to allow traffic from the entire VPC CIDR block
questions.explanation: Referencing security groups rather than IP ranges is the AWS best practice. The EC2 SG allows inbound on the app port only from the ALB's SG. The RDS SG allows inbound on the DB port only from the EC2 SG. This is least privilege: each tier only accepts traffic from the specific upstream tier, and rules update automatically as instances scale.

questions.question: A company wants to build a serverless REST API that calls Lambda functions. The API must handle authentication using JWT tokens. Which AWS service combination is CORRECT?
options: ALB + Lambda Target Group + Cognito User Pool
API Gateway + Lambda + Cognito Authorizer (or Lambda Authorizer)
CloudFront + Lambda@Edge + IAM authentication
Elastic Beanstalk + Lambda + DynamoDB
questions.explanation: API Gateway integrates natively with Lambda as a backend and supports authorizers for authentication. A Cognito User Pool Authorizer validates JWT tokens from Cognito. A Lambda Authorizer provides custom JWT validation logic. API Gateway handles routing, throttling, and caching. Lambda@Edge is for CDN edge logic, not REST API hosting.

questions.question: A company needs its RDS database to be available even if hardware fails in the primary Availability Zone, with automatic failover and minimal application changes. Which feature provides this?
options: RDS Read Replica in a different AZ
RDS Multi-AZ deployment with synchronous standby replication
Manual snapshot restore to a new instance in another AZ
RDS Cross-Region Replication
questions.explanation: RDS Multi-AZ maintains a synchronous standby replica in a different AZ. If the primary fails, RDS automatically promotes the standby with failover typically completing in 60-120 seconds. The application uses the same DNS endpoint — no code changes needed. Read Replicas are asynchronous and not automatic failover targets. Snapshots require manual intervention.

questions.question: A company has a global user base. They want to improve performance for users accessing a dynamic API hosted in us-east-1. The API cannot be cached. Which service reduces latency for global users?
options: CloudFront with a custom origin pointing to the API
AWS Global Accelerator with an ALB endpoint in us-east-1
Route 53 latency-based routing to us-east-1
Deploy the API in multiple regions using DynamoDB Global Tables
questions.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator routes user traffic to the AWS global network at the nearest edge location, reducing internet hops and improving TCP/UDP performance for dynamic (uncacheable) content. CloudFront is best for cacheable content. Global Accelerator uses anycast IPs and directs traffic over AWS's optimized backbone. Route 53 latency routing still sends users over the public internet to the origin.

questions.question: A company uses CloudFormation to deploy infrastructure. A developer accidentally deleted the production stack. Which feature would have prevented the deletion?
options: CloudFormation drift detection
CloudFormation StackSets
CloudFormation termination protection enabled on the stack
AWS Config rules monitoring the CloudFormation stack
questions.explanation: CloudFormation termination protection prevents a stack from being accidentally deleted. When enabled, any attempt to delete the stack fails until protection is explicitly disabled. This is a simple but critical guard for production stacks. Drift detection identifies configuration differences but doesn't prevent deletion. StackSets deploys across accounts/regions.

questions.question: An application needs to send transactional emails at scale with guaranteed delivery and bounce/complaint handling. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?
options: Amazon SNS with email subscriptions
Amazon SES (Simple Email Service)
Amazon Pinpoint with email channel
Lambda triggering an SMTP relay on EC2
questions.explanation: Amazon SES is AWS's managed email sending service designed for transactional and marketing email at scale. It handles SMTP, bounce/complaint notifications, dedicated IPs, and email deliverability. SNS email is for notifications/alerts, not transactional emails. Pinpoint is a marketing engagement platform. Self-managing SMTP on EC2 creates unnecessary operational overhead.

questions.question: A company wants to restrict access to an S3 bucket so that only users from a specific AWS Organization can access it, regardless of IAM permissions. Which feature enables this?
options: S3 ACL with an organization-wide condition
S3 bucket policy with aws:PrincipalOrgID condition key
IAM permission boundary applied to all organization users
S3 Block Public Access settings
questions.explanation: The aws:PrincipalOrgID global condition key in an S3 bucket policy allows access only when the principal belongs to the specified AWS Organization. This ensures that even if credentials leak outside the organization, they cannot access the bucket. Permission boundaries apply to individual principals, not organization-wide. S3 Block Public Access blocks anonymous access but not cross-account access.

questions.question: A Lambda function processes images uploaded to S3. Very large images require over 15 minutes of processing — beyond Lambda's maximum timeout. What is the BEST architectural approach?
options: Increase Lambda memory allocation to speed up processing
Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate chunked processing with multiple Lambda invocations
Move the processing to EC2 with Auto Scaling
Switch to Lambda container images with a larger deployment package
questions.explanation: AWS Step Functions can orchestrate a multi-step workflow where large images are split into processable chunks, each handled by a separate Lambda invocation within the 15-minute limit. Step Functions manages state, retries, and parallel execution. Simply increasing memory speeds up CPU-bound tasks but doesn't solve the architectural timeout constraint. EC2 would work but loses the serverless benefits.

questions.question: A company stores sensitive configuration data (database passwords, API keys) that EC2 instances and Lambda functions need. The data must be encrypted at rest, version-controlled, and access-audited. Which service is MOST appropriate?
options: Store in S3 with SSE-KMS encryption
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with SecureString type backed by KMS
Hardcode in EC2 user data scripts
Store in DynamoDB with encryption enabled
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with SecureString type encrypts values using KMS, supports versioning, and logs all access in CloudTrail. It integrates natively with EC2, Lambda, ECS, and other services. AWS Secrets Manager is also valid (with automatic rotation), but Parameter Store is free for standard parameters. S3 can store secrets but lacks the purpose-built access model. DynamoDB is a database, not a secrets store.

questions.question: An application experiences traffic spikes lasting 2-3 minutes, several times per day. The workload runs on EC2. Which Auto Scaling approach responds FASTEST to these brief spikes?
options: Scheduled scaling actions set to specific spike times
Simple scaling policy triggered by CloudWatch alarms
Predictive scaling using ML to forecast traffic
Step scaling policy combined with a warm pool of pre-initialized instances
questions.explanation: A warm pool keeps pre-initialized, stopped EC2 instances that can be launched within seconds rather than the typical 3-5 minutes for cold starts. Step scaling (which adds multiple instances based on alarm breach magnitude) combined with warm pool provides the fastest response for sub-5-minute spikes. Scheduled scaling works when spike times are predictable. Predictive scaling is ML-based and best for recurring patterns.

questions.question: A company wants to enforce MFA on all IAM users and deny all API calls unless MFA has been used. Which IAM mechanism achieves this?
options: Set a password policy requiring MFA registration
Attach an IAM policy with a Deny statement using the aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition key set to false
Enable AWS Config rule to check for MFA
Use CloudTrail to alert on non-MFA API calls
questions.explanation: An IAM policy with Deny on all actions ('*') with condition aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent: false blocks all API calls when MFA has NOT been used. This is the standard IAM pattern to enforce MFA. The user can log in but cannot do anything until they authenticate with MFA. Password policy enforces MFA registration but not per-request enforcement. Config and CloudTrail detect/alert but don't block.

questions.question: A company wants to run containerized microservices without managing EC2 instances or clusters, paying only for the resources used by running containers. Which service meets these requirements?
options: Amazon ECS with EC2 launch type
Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate launch type
Amazon EKS with self-managed node groups
Amazon ECR with Auto Scaling
questions.explanation: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers. With ECS Fargate, you define tasks and services — AWS manages the underlying infrastructure. You pay per vCPU and memory used by running containers, with no EC2 instances to manage, patch, or scale. ECS EC2 launch type requires managing EC2 instances. EKS with self-managed nodes requires managing EC2 nodes. ECR is a container registry, not compute.

questions.question: A company's application generates reports that take 10 minutes to produce. Users submit requests through a web frontend and need to be notified when their report is ready. Which architecture pattern handles this correctly?
options: Synchronous HTTP call from the frontend that waits 10 minutes for the response
Frontend submits job to SQS, worker processes asynchronously, SNS/email notifies user when complete
Frontend polls a Lambda function every 5 seconds to check status
Use API Gateway timeout extension to wait 10 minutes
questions.explanation: Asynchronous processing with a queue decouples the request from the long-running job. The frontend submits a job to SQS and immediately returns a job ID. A worker picks up the job, processes it, and when complete sends a notification via SNS or SES. API Gateway has a 29-second timeout. Polling every 5 seconds creates unnecessary load. Lambda has a 15-minute max but this still doesn't solve the synchronous UX problem.

questions.question: An Aurora MySQL cluster needs to handle a sudden 10x increase in read traffic due to a promotional campaign. The write workload stays constant. What is the QUICKEST way to scale read capacity?
options: Add more Aurora Read Replicas (up to 15) to the cluster
Promote an existing read replica to become a standalone writer
Enable Aurora Global Database for cross-region reads
Upgrade to a larger DB instance class
questions.explanation: Aurora supports up to 15 read replicas sharing the same underlying storage (unlike RDS replicas which have their own copies). Adding replicas is fast and the cluster reader endpoint automatically distributes reads. Aurora replicas have minimal lag (typically <100ms). Promoting a replica removes read capacity. Global Database adds cross-region latency overhead. Upgrading instance class helps per-replica capacity but doesn't distribute load.

questions.question: A company has multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. They need to deploy a standard CloudTrail configuration across all accounts and regions. What is the MOST efficient approach?
options: Deploy a CloudFormation template in each account manually
Use CloudFormation StackSets with Organizations integration to deploy across all accounts and regions
Write a Lambda function to deploy CloudTrail in each account
Use AWS Config to detect missing CloudTrail and send alerts
questions.explanation: CloudFormation StackSets with AWS Organizations integration (service-managed permissions) automatically deploys stack instances to all accounts and specified regions in the organization. New accounts joining the organization automatically get the stack deployed. This is the most scalable, automated approach for multi-account configuration management. Manual deployments and Lambda scripts don't scale with organizational growth.

questions.question: A company stores financial transaction data in DynamoDB. They need to maintain a history of all changes to each item for compliance auditing. Which feature enables this WITHOUT custom application code changes?
options: DynamoDB on-demand backups
DynamoDB Streams captured by Lambda writing each change to S3
DynamoDB Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR)
DynamoDB Global Tables
questions.explanation: DynamoDB Streams captures a time-ordered sequence of every item-level modification. A Lambda function triggered by the stream can write each change event to S3, forming an immutable audit trail. PITR allows restore to any point in time but doesn't provide a browsable change history. On-demand backups create snapshots but not change logs. Global Tables replicate data across regions but don't maintain change history.

questions.question: A company needs to run a batch processing job that is not time-critical but must complete eventually at the lowest cost. The job can tolerate interruption. Which EC2 purchasing option is MOST cost-effective?
options: On-Demand Instances
Reserved Instances (1-year, no upfront)
Spot Instances with checkpointing and Spot interruption handling
Dedicated Hosts
questions.explanation: Spot Instances offer up to 90% discount versus On-Demand pricing. For fault-tolerant, non-time-critical batch workloads that can checkpoint progress and handle 2-minute interruption notices, Spot Instances are the optimal choice. On-Demand is most expensive per hour. Reserved Instances save 30-70% but require upfront commitment for predictable workloads. Dedicated Hosts are the most expensive option.

questions.question: An application serving both HTTP and HTTPS traffic needs to redirect all HTTP requests to HTTPS at the load balancer level. Which load balancer type supports this redirect rule?
options: Network Load Balancer (NLB)
Classic Load Balancer (CLB)
Application Load Balancer (ALB) with a redirect listener rule
Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)
questions.explanation: ALB supports listener rules with redirect actions. You create an HTTP listener (port 80) with a redirect rule that sends a 301 response redirecting to HTTPS (port 443). This happens at the load balancer, saving a round trip to the backend. NLB operates at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) and cannot inspect or modify HTTP requests. CLB has limited rule support. GWLB is for third-party network appliances.

questions.question: A company uses AWS CloudTrail. A security team wants to ensure CloudTrail logs cannot be modified or deleted by anyone, including administrators. Which feature provides this guarantee?
options: Enable MFA Delete on the S3 bucket storing CloudTrail logs
Enable CloudTrail log file validation and store logs in an S3 bucket with Object Lock in Compliance mode
Encrypt CloudTrail logs with a KMS CMK
Set S3 bucket ACLs to private on the CloudTrail log bucket
questions.explanation: S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode prevents anyone — including the root account — from deleting or modifying locked objects before their retention period expires. Combined with CloudTrail log file validation (SHA-256 hash chain), you can detect any tampering. Log file validation proves logs haven't been altered after delivery. KMS encryption protects confidentiality but not integrity. ACLs control access but administrators can still delete logs.

questions.question: A company's web application experiences sudden traffic surges that can 10x normal load within 30 seconds. The application tier is stateless. Which approach handles sub-minute scaling BEST?
options: EC2 Auto Scaling with a 5-minute warm-up period
AWS Lambda with an ALB — Lambda scales instantly to thousands of concurrent executions
Pre-scaled EC2 fleet with reserved capacity for peak
Elastic Beanstalk with rolling updates
questions.explanation: Lambda scales from 0 to thousands of concurrent executions in seconds. For stateless workloads that can run within Lambda's execution model, this provides instant scaling beyond what EC2 Auto Scaling can achieve in 30 seconds. Lambda with ALB is a valid production pattern. Pre-scaling wastes cost at normal load. Auto Scaling has a 3-5 minute EC2 launch time.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate an on-premises Oracle database to AWS with minimal downtime. Which service handles heterogeneous database migration with ongoing replication during the cutover window?
options: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) with Schema Conversion Tool
AWS Snowball for database file transfer
Manually export/import using Oracle Data Pump
AWS DataSync
questions.explanation: AWS DMS migrates databases to AWS with minimal downtime using Change Data Capture (CDC) for ongoing replication after the initial full load. The Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) handles schema conversion for heterogeneous migrations (e.g., Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL). During migration, the source remains online until cutover. Snowball is for bulk data transfer. Data Pump requires downtime. DataSync is for file-based storage.

questions.question: A company needs to share VPC resources between AWS accounts in the same AWS Organization without using VPC peering. Which feature allows subnets to be shared across accounts?
options: VPC Peering between accounts
AWS Transit Gateway
AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) to share subnets from a central VPC
VPC Endpoints with service sharing
questions.explanation: AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) allows sharing subnets from a central 'owner' account with 'participant' accounts in the same Organization. Participant accounts can launch EC2 instances, RDS, and other resources into the shared subnet without needing their own VPC. This simplifies networking and reduces costs by eliminating duplicate infrastructure. VPC Peering connects separate VPCs; RAM shares subnets within one VPC.

questions.question: A company needs to expose an internal service running on EC2 to another company's VPC without establishing full VPC peering. Which feature enables this securely?
options: VPC Peering between the two companies' VPCs
AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint Service) with a Network Load Balancer
AWS Direct Connect between the two companies
Internet Gateway with security group rules
questions.explanation: AWS PrivateLink allows exposing a service to other VPCs or AWS accounts without VPC peering, internet exposure, or overlapping CIDR concerns. The provider creates a VPC Endpoint Service backed by a Network Load Balancer. The consumer creates an Interface VPC Endpoint in their VPC. Traffic never leaves the AWS network. VPC Peering exposes the entire VPC, not just one service.

questions.question: A serverless application with API Gateway and Lambda is seeing a high percentage of 429 errors from Lambda throttling. What are TWO appropriate remediation steps?
options: Increase API Gateway timeout to 30 seconds
Request a Lambda concurrency limit increase and implement exponential backoff with jitter in clients
Move to EC2 instances to avoid Lambda limits
Enable API Gateway caching for all endpoints
questions.explanation: Lambda has per-region concurrency limits (default 1000). Requesting a limit increase via AWS Support directly addresses the capacity issue. Implementing exponential backoff with jitter in clients handles transient throttling gracefully without overwhelming Lambda during bursts. API Gateway caching helps for GET requests but not all endpoints. Moving to EC2 loses serverless benefits and is disproportionate.

questions.question: A company needs to query data stored in S3 using standard SQL without loading it into a database. The data is in Parquet format, partitioned by date. Which service handles this?
options: Amazon RDS with S3 integration
Amazon Athena with a Glue Data Catalog table definition
Amazon Redshift with S3 COPY command
AWS Glue ETL job writing results to DynamoDB
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena is a serverless query service that uses SQL (Presto) to query data directly in S3. AWS Glue Data Catalog defines the schema and partition structure. Athena reads only specific Parquet files matching query filters (partition pruning), minimizing scan and cost. You pay per TB scanned. RDS and Redshift require loading data first. Glue ETL is for transformation, not ad-hoc querying.

questions.question: A company uses IAM Identity Center (SSO). An audit requirement mandates that all administrative actions in all AWS accounts must be logged with the caller's identity. Which service provides this centrally?
options: AWS Config aggregator across all accounts
AWS CloudTrail Organization Trail writing to a central S3 bucket in a log archive account
Amazon CloudWatch Logs cross-account subscription
VPC Flow Logs from all accounts sent to S3
questions.explanation: An AWS CloudTrail Organization Trail automatically enables CloudTrail in all accounts in the organization, with all events delivered to a central S3 bucket in a log archive account. This creates an immutable, centralized audit log of all API activity including the IAM Identity Center caller identity. Config aggregates configuration state, not API call logs. VPC Flow Logs capture network traffic, not API calls.

questions.question: A company needs to temporarily grant external auditors read access to specific S3 buckets. The auditors have their own AWS account. What is the MOST secure approach?
options: Create IAM users for each auditor and share credentials via email
Create a cross-account IAM role with read-only S3 permissions and share the role ARN with the auditors to assume
Make the S3 buckets publicly accessible with signed URLs
Create a new AWS account for the auditors with root access
questions.explanation: Cross-account IAM roles are the AWS-recommended pattern for temporary cross-account access. You create a role in your account with the required permissions and a trust policy allowing the auditor's account to assume it. The auditors call sts:AssumeRole to get temporary credentials — no permanent credentials are created or shared. When access is no longer needed, delete the role. Sharing IAM user credentials is a security anti-pattern.

questions.question: An application reads configuration from Parameter Store at startup and restarts frequently, causing high API call volume and throttling. What should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Switch to environment variables stored in EC2 User Data
Use AWS AppConfig with a caching client, or implement parameter caching in the application
Upgrade Parameter Store to Advanced tier for higher throughput
Move all parameters to S3 and read from there
questions.explanation: AWS AppConfig is built for application configuration with native client-side caching and validation. For Parameter Store, implementing a cache (cache parameters at startup for 5-10 minutes) dramatically reduces GetParameter API calls. The Advanced tier increases throughput limits but adds cost — caching is free and more architecturally sound. Reading from S3 lacks versioning, encryption, and audit features of Parameter Store.

questions.question: A media company needs to transcode uploaded videos into multiple formats. Jobs take 5-20 minutes each and thousands of videos are uploaded daily. Which architecture is MOST scalable and cost-effective?
options: A single large EC2 instance running transcoding software
S3 upload event triggers Lambda, but Lambda cannot handle 20-minute jobs without Step Functions
S3 upload event to SQS queue consumed by ECS Fargate tasks that auto-scale based on queue depth
Store videos in EFS and batch process with a Glue ETL job
questions.explanation: S3 event → SQS → ECS Fargate with auto-scaling based on queue depth is the ideal pattern for long-running batch jobs. Fargate tasks pick up jobs from SQS, process them (no Lambda 15-minute limit), and scale out as the queue grows. Fargate is serverless — no EC2 management. A single EC2 creates a bottleneck. Lambda can't handle 20-minute jobs reliably. EFS/Glue doesn't leverage the event-driven pattern.

questions.question: A company needs to protect an ALB-fronted web application from SQL injection and XSS attacks. Which service provides this protection at the load balancer level?
options: AWS Shield Standard
Security Groups on the ALB
AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) attached to the ALB
Amazon GuardDuty
questions.explanation: AWS WAF operates at Layer 7 and can inspect HTTP request content (body, headers, URI) for SQL injection and XSS patterns using AWS Managed Rules or custom rules. WAF can be attached directly to ALB, CloudFront, or API Gateway. Shield Standard protects against DDoS volumetric attacks at Layers 3/4, not application-layer attacks. Security Groups are Layer 4. GuardDuty is threat detection, not a blocking WAF.

questions.question: A company is designing a multi-tier application (web, app, database tiers). Each tier should only communicate with the adjacent tier. Which configuration BEST enforces this isolation?
options: Place all tiers in the same subnet with one security group
Create separate security groups per tier; reference the upstream tier's SG in inbound rules rather than IP ranges
Use NACLs on each subnet to block inter-tier traffic
Use VPN tunnels between each tier for encrypted communication
questions.explanation: Using security group references (SG-to-SG rules) enforces tier isolation dynamically — when instances scale in/out, new instances automatically inherit SG membership and access controls update without IP changes. App tier's SG allows inbound only from web tier's SG; DB tier's SG allows inbound only from app tier's SG. NACLs are stateless and harder to maintain. VPNs are for inter-network connectivity.

questions.question: A company wants to run analytics queries on petabytes of structured data with complex JOINs requiring sub-minute response times. Which AWS service is DESIGNED for this workload?
options: Amazon DynamoDB with GSIs
Amazon Athena with S3 data lake
Amazon Redshift
Amazon RDS Aurora with read replicas
questions.explanation: Amazon Redshift is a petabyte-scale columnar data warehouse optimized for complex analytical queries (OLAP) with massive parallel processing (MPP). It handles complex JOINs and aggregations over billions of rows far more efficiently than row-based databases. DynamoDB excels at low-latency single-item access. Athena is good for ad-hoc queries but slower at this scale. RDS is OLTP, not OLAP.

questions.question: An application on EC2 has an IAM role with s3:* and ec2:* permissions. The application only reads from one specific S3 bucket. What change enforces least privilege?
options: Add a Deny policy for all other services
Remove ec2:* entirely and replace s3:* with s3:GetObject restricted to the specific bucket ARN
Move the permissions to an IAM user attached to the instance
Add a condition key restricting actions by source IP
questions.explanation: Least privilege means granting only the exact permissions required. Replace s3:* with s3:GetObject on the specific bucket ARN (arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/*) and remove ec2:* entirely since the application doesn't need EC2 API calls. This minimizes blast radius if the instance is compromised. Using a Deny policy on top of broad Allow is less clean than not granting the permissions. IAM users on EC2 is an anti-pattern.

questions.question: A company has an active-passive DR setup across two AWS regions. The RTO is 15 minutes and RPO is 1 minute. Which database replication approach meets the RPO requirement?
options: Daily RDS snapshots copied to the secondary region
RDS cross-region read replica with replication lag under 1 minute
Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) with 1-minute granularity
Amazon Aurora Global Database with typical replication lag under 1 second
questions.explanation: Aurora Global Database provides cross-region replication with typical lag under 1 second (well within 1-minute RPO). In a disaster, the secondary region can be promoted in under 1 minute (within RTO). Standard RDS cross-region replicas have higher lag and slower promotion. Daily snapshots produce RPO of up to 24 hours. PITR restoration itself takes minutes to hours.

questions.question: A company needs to access AWS service APIs (SSM, EC2 API, STS) from private subnets without routing traffic over the internet. Which is the CORRECT solution?
options: Deploy a NAT Gateway for all AWS API traffic
Create Interface VPC Endpoints (powered by AWS PrivateLink) for the required AWS services
Use Gateway Endpoints for all AWS services
Set up a bastion host to proxy all AWS API calls
questions.explanation: Interface VPC Endpoints create elastic network interfaces (ENIs) in your subnet that provide private access to AWS service APIs via AWS PrivateLink — no internet, no NAT required. Gateway Endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB (free). Interface endpoints cover most other AWS services (hourly charge + data processing fee). NAT Gateway routes traffic over the internet and incurs higher data transfer costs.

questions.question: A company needs to track all API calls including read-only calls, store logs for 7 years for compliance, and ensure logs are tamper-proof. What is the COMPLETE solution?
options: Enable CloudTrail management events only and store in S3 Standard
Enable CloudTrail with management and data events; store in S3 with Object Lock Compliance mode, Glacier archival lifecycle, and log file validation enabled
Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query all API calls
Enable AWS Config with 7-year retention
questions.explanation: Comprehensive compliance logging requires: (1) CloudTrail with management events (all API calls including reads), (2) Log file validation to detect tampering via SHA-256 hashes, (3) S3 Object Lock Compliance mode to prevent deletion/modification for 7 years, (4) S3 lifecycle to transition to Glacier for cost-effective long-term storage. CloudWatch Logs lacks tamper-proof guarantees. Config tracks resource state, not all API calls.

questions.question: A company is migrating a monolith to microservices on AWS. Services need to communicate synchronously with low latency. Which AWS service is BEST for synchronous inter-service HTTP communication?
options: Amazon SQS for all service-to-service calls
Amazon SNS for broadcasting requests
Amazon API Gateway (HTTP APIs) or ALB for service-to-service HTTP/HTTPS calls
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for all inter-service messaging
questions.explanation: Synchronous inter-service communication requires request-response semantics. API Gateway HTTP APIs (lower latency, lower cost than REST APIs) or ALB with path-based routing to different microservices is the standard AWS pattern. API Gateway adds authentication, throttling, and request transformation. ALB is simpler for internal traffic. SQS and Kinesis are asynchronous. SNS is a pub/sub broadcast system.
